name: io.github.MISHHF93/atlas-explain
title: ATLAS Explain
description: Market jargon in plain language: terms, official figures, crypto prices and charts, headlines.

tools.name: explain_term
tools.description: The plain-language meaning of a market or economics term from ATLAS Explain's glossary, such as stop-limit order, yield curve, inflation or P/E. Use it when someone asks what a term means. Up to three closest terms, each with its glossary group. Education only.

term.description: The term or phrase to look up.

tools.name: browse_glossary
tools.description: List ATLAS Explain's learning path (topics in order, each with its terms) or every glossary term in one group. Use it to suggest what to learn next, or to find the right term to explain.

topic.description: Optional learning-path topic or glossary group, for example 'orders', 'risk', 'rates', 'futures'. Leave empty for the whole path.

tools.name: asset_details
tools.description: What one asset is, where and when it trades, and its latest official figure or price with source and time, or why no price is shown. Use it when someone asks about a specific coin, stock, ETF, currency, rate or index. Covers crypto, US stocks and ETFs, currencies, interest rates, energy, indices, futures and options.

tools.name: official_figures
tools.description: Official figures with source and date: US Treasury yields, ECB and Bank of Canada rates, EIA energy prices, and SEC-filed company figures. Use it for rates, yields, exchange rates or a company's reported results. The SEC figures cover revenue, net income, earnings per share and shares outstanding for about 30 large US companies and ETFs. Optional search by name or symbol.

query.description: Optional name or symbol, for example '10-year', 'EUR', 'AAPL'.

tools.name: crypto_prices
tools.description: Current prices and the change over the last 24 hours for ten major coins, biggest moves first, with when they were collected. Use it for how crypto is doing today, or one coin's price. Coins: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, Cardano, Dogecoin, Litecoin, Polkadot, Chainlink and Avalanche, each with its last 24 hours of hourly closes. Refreshed about every 10 minutes by ATLAS Explain's data job from Kraken's public market data (CoinGecko as backup) and served from ATLAS Explain's own data site.

coin.description: Optional coin name or symbol, for example 'BTC' or 'Ethereum'.

tools.name: price_history
tools.description: How a coin moved over 24 hours, 7 days or 30 days: start, end, change, high and low with their times. Use it when someone asks how a coin moved or wants a price chart. From the hourly closes on ATLAS Explain's own data site (refreshed about every 10 minutes). Describes the past only; never a forecast.

coin.description: Coin name or symbol, for example 'BTC'.

tools.name: todays_headlines
tools.description: Recent market headlines and official press releases, each with publisher, link and time. Use it for what's in the news, optionally about one company or coin. Sources: official press releases from the Federal Reserve, SEC, CFTC, ECB, Bank of Canada and Bank of England, and the GDELT Project's news index. News stories older than 36 hours and releases older than 4 days are never returned.

about.description: Optional company, coin or word, for example 'Nvidia' or 'Bitcoin'.

tools.name: economy_snapshot
tools.description: Headline economic figures with period, change and source: inflation, unemployment, policy rates and US public debt, plus the next rate decisions. Use it for how the economy is doing, or one topic. Covers US CPI over 12 months and unemployment (Bureau of Labor Statistics), the effective federal funds rate with the Fed's target range and SOFR (New York Fed), euro-area inflation and the ECB deposit rate (ECB) and euro-area unemployment (Eurostat), Canada's inflation and unemployment (Statistics Canada), policy rate and the chartered banks' posted prime, 5-year mortgage and 5-year GIC rates (Bank of Canada), US national average savings and CD rates (FDIC), the UK's quoted 2- and 5-year fixed mortgage rates (Bank of England), the euro area's cost of borrowing for a home and household deposit rate (ECB), the UK's inflation and unemployment (Office for National Statistics) and Bank Rate (Bank of England), and US public debt (Treasury), each with about a year of history. Optional filter by topic, for example 'canada inflation', 'uk', 'mortgage' or 'savings'.

topic.description: Optional topic, for example 'inflation', 'jobs', 'rates', 'debt', 'euro' or 'canada'. Leave empty for all.

tools.name: economic_calendar
tools.description: Dates of the next interest-rate decisions by the Federal Reserve, the European Central Bank, the Bank of Canada and the Bank of England, with what happens on the day. Use it for when the next Fed, ECB, Bank of Canada or Bank of England meeting is. From each bank's own published calendar. Dates only: it never guesses the outcome. Optional filter by central bank.

bank.description: Optional: 'Fed', 'ECB', 'Bank of Canada' or 'Bank of England'. Leave empty for all.

tools.name: market_depth
tools.description: A coin's best bid and ask, bid-ask spread, order-book depth, and the slippage of filling an order of a given size. Use it to explain spreads, liquidity or trading costs with real numbers. For the ten coins ATLAS Explain follows, from Kraken's public market data; the spread is refreshed every few minutes and the order book about every 10 minutes. Explains how markets work; never suggests a trade.

coin.description: Coin name or symbol, for example 'BTC'.

tools.name: evidence_brief
tools.description: Everything ATLAS Explain knows about one asset on one page, each fact sourced, plus what the facts don't tell you. Use it when someone wants the full picture on a coin, company, currency or rate. Includes what it is, its latest figures or price, how it moved over 7 days and how easily it trades (coins), the economic backdrop and the next rate decision, headlines that name it, terms to know, and what people commonly look at for this kind of asset. Facts only: it never recommends, rates or forecasts anything.

asset.description: Name or symbol, for example 'Bitcoin', 'AAPL', 'EUR/USD' or '10-year'.

tools.name: notable_today
tools.description: What stands out in today's data, each with its source and the rule that picked it: unusual crypto moves, a flat or inverted yield curve, rate decisions this week, changed economic figures. Use it for what's happening or what's worth knowing today. Also lists new official releases and what was checked but found ordinary. Describes the past only; never a forecast or a suggestion.

tools.name: upcoming_events
tools.description: The next scheduled market events with exact times and a countdown: Fed, ECB, Bank of Canada and Bank of England rate decisions and the US inflation, jobs and producer-price releases. Use it for what's coming up, or when the next CPI or jobs report or rate decision is. Each event has the latest related figure and 'if this happens' explainers for each possible outcome, from the banks' and the BLS's own calendars. It never says which outcome will happen. Optional filter: 'rates' or 'data'.

only.description: Optional: only rate decisions, or only data releases.

tools.name: money_maths
tools.description: Works out compound growth, what a fee costs over the years, what inflation does to cash, or how holding more things changes how much a mix swings, from numbers the person gives. Use it to show how money grows or shrinks over time with their own example. Pure arithmetic, drawn as a chart they can change in Claude; the rate is their assumption, never a forecast or a suggestion.

monthly.description: Optional amount added each month (compound_growth, fees).

rate_pct.description: Yearly return the person wants to assume, in percent (compound_growth, fees).

fee_pct.description: Yearly fee in percent of the balance (fees).

inflation_pct.description: Yearly inflation to assume, in percent (inflation).

volatility_pct.description: How much one holding swings in a year, in percent (diversification).

correlation.description: How closely holdings move together, -1 to 1 (diversification).

holdings.description: Show up to this many holdings, 2 to 100 (diversification; default 20).

tools.name: scam_red_flags
tools.description: The warning signs of investment fraud regulators describe, which of them a message or offer shows, where to check a seller's registration and where to report, plus recent official fraud actions. Use it when someone asks whether an offer, message or 'opportunity' looks like a scam. It points out warning signs; it never says something is or isn't a scam, and the text given is not kept.

pitch.description: Optional: the message, ad or offer the person received, in their words or pasted. Leave empty for the full list of warning signs.

tools.name: treasury_auctions
tools.description: Upcoming US Treasury auctions and the latest results: what is sold, how much, the yield it set and how much demand there was. Use it to explain how the US government borrows, or what bid-to-cover and auction yields mean. From TreasuryDirect, refreshed every 6 hours. Describes auctions that are announced or done; never predicts a result. Optional filter: bills, notes, bonds or TIPS.

kind.description: Optional: 'bills', 'notes', 'bonds' or 'TIPS'. Leave empty for all.

tools.name: compare_countries
tools.description: GDP growth, inflation, unemployment and GDP per person for the G20 countries and the EU, with the year of each figure, from the World Bank. Use it to compare economies or put one country's figures in context. Actual published values only (World Development Indicators, CC BY 4.0), updated daily; never a projection. Optional: one indicator and a list of countries.

indicator.description: Optional: 'gdp growth', 'inflation', 'unemployment' or 'gdp per person'. Leave empty for all four.

countries.description: Optional: country names or codes separated by commas, for example 'Canada, Japan, Germany'. Leave empty for the whole G20.

tools.name: data_series
tools.description: Clean dated rows of official economic data, with source and licence, for making a chart, spreadsheet, table or report. Use it when someone wants the numbers themselves, or to build something from them. Covers US inflation, unemployment, the fed funds rate, SOFR and debt; euro-area, Canadian and UK inflation and unemployment; the ECB, Bank of Canada and Bank of England rates; and World Bank GDP growth, inflation, unemployment and GDP per person for the G20. Also returns CSV. Leave empty for the list. Never crypto or stock prices.

series.description: Optional: one to four series ids or names, separated by commas, for example 'us_cpi, uk_bank_rate' or 'world_inflation'. Leave empty to list what's available.

countries.description: For world_ series: up to six G20 country names or codes, for example 'Japan, Germany'. Defaults to the United States.

tools.name: learning_hub
tools.description: Opens the ATLAS Explain learning path as a hub: three quick questions per topic from the glossary to check understanding, and spaced review, where a passed topic comes back after 1, 7 and 28 days. Use it when someone wants to practise, test what they've learned, review, or see their learning progress. Progress stays on their device. For teaching a topic term by term, use browse_glossary or the learn_next prompt.

topic.description: Optional learning-path topic to start a check on, for example 'rates' or 'saving'. Leave empty for the whole path.

tools.name: learning_check
tools.description: Three multiple-choice questions on one learning-path topic, each a glossary description with the term's name blanked out. Called by the learning hub view; to quiz someone in the chat, use the quiz_me prompt instead.

topic.description: The learning-path topic id, for example 'rates'.

seed.description: Any whole number; the same seed gives the same questions.

tools.name: debt_payoff
tools.description: Works out how long it takes to pay off several debts with one monthly amount, and the interest paid, by two methods: avalanche (extra money to the highest rate first) and snowball (extra money to the smallest balance first), month by month. Use it when someone asks how to plan paying off credit cards or loans, which order to pay them in, or how much interest they'd pay. Pure arithmetic on their numbers; it compares the methods and never says which to choose.

debts.description: Each debt: a short name, the balance, the yearly interest rate in percent and the minimum monthly payment.

name.description: A short name, for example 'Visa' or 'Car loan'.

rate_pct.description: The yearly interest rate, in percent.

monthly_budget.description: The total that can go to these debts each month, at least the minimums added up.

tools.name: whats_changed
tools.description: What changed in the economy since a date: each official figure that moved (inflation, unemployment, policy rates, US debt for the US, euro area, Canada and the UK), written as 'went from … to …' with its source, plus the Federal Reserve, Bank of Canada, ECB and Bank of England statements and speeches published since, and the next rate decisions. Use it when someone asks what's new, what happened this week, or what they missed since a date. Up to 90 days back. Describes the past only; never a forecast.

topic.description: What to look at. Default all.

since.description: Optional: the date to compare with, YYYY-MM-DD, at most 90 days back.

days.description: Optional instead of since: how many days back, 1 to 90. Default 7.

tools.name: inflation_calculator
tools.description: Works out what an amount of money from one year is worth in another, from the official consumer price index of the US (1913 on, Bureau of Labor Statistics), Canada (1914 on, Statistics Canada), the UK (1988 on, Office for National Statistics) or the euro area (1997 on, ECB), as yearly averages. Use it when someone asks what money from the past is worth today, how much prices have risen since a year, or what inflation did to their savings. Describes the past only; never a forecast.

amount.description: The amount of money, in that country's currency.

from_year.description: The year the amount is from.

to_year.description: The year to compare with. Defaults to the latest full year.

country.description: US, CA (Canada), UK or EA (the euro area). Ask if unsure; defaults to the US.

tools.name: rate_change_impact
tools.description: Works out what a change in interest rates would do to someone's own variable-rate mortgage payment, HELOC interest, savings interest or GIC/CD renewal, to the cent, and which central bank drives that product (Canada: Bank of Canada; US: the Federal Reserve). Use it when someone asks what a cut or a rise would mean for them. Pure arithmetic on the numbers they give; for reference it also shows today's posted prime or GIC rate in Canada, or the US national average savings or CD rate. It never says whether a change will happen.

balance.description: Amount owed (mortgage, HELOC) or held (savings, GIC/CD), in dollars.

rate_pct.description: The rate today, in percent a year.

change_pts.description: The change to work out, in percentage points: -0.25 for a quarter-point cut, 0.5 for a half-point rise.

months.description: Mortgage: months left to pay it off (default 300). GIC/CD: the term in months (default 12).

country.description: Where the product is. Decides which central bank it follows and, for mortgages, the usual compounding. Ask if unsure.

compounding.description: Mortgage only. Defaults to semi-annual in Canada, monthly in the US.

tools.name: decision_explainer
tools.description: What the Federal Reserve, the Bank of Canada, the European Central Bank or the Bank of England decided at its latest rate decision (or the one before), how the official statement's wording changed from the previous one, word for word, and what the bank itself says it is watching, quoted with links. Use it when someone asks what a central bank just did or what changed. From the banks' own statements; it never says what the bank will do next.

bank.description: fed (Federal Reserve), boc (Bank of Canada), ecb (European Central Bank) or boe (Bank of England).

date.description: Optional: the decision date, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to the latest; the one before is also kept.

tools.name: speech_tracker
tools.description: Recent speeches and remarks by Federal Reserve, Bank of Canada, ECB or Bank of England policymakers: who spoke, when, the title, the bank's own one-line description and a link to the full text. Use it when someone asks what central bankers have been saying. Descriptions are the bank's own words, attributed; nothing is added or interpreted.

bank.description: fed (Federal Reserve), boc (Bank of Canada), ecb (European Central Bank) or boe (Bank of England).

days.description: How far back to look, in days (default 30, at most 90).
